narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'take refuge in him' - the interior that stops fighting the king and shelters in him. Type (102) is affect: a movement of feeling and reliance, not a bare deed or a reasoned stance. Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior spring behind the refuge-taking; after a whole psalm of wrath and revolt it simply names the sheltering, not its cause. Seat (104) resolves to none: the operation is not organ-located - no faculty is switched on; the whole person shelters. Bearer (105) is 'all who trust' (inferred): the interior addressed is everyone who ends the rebellion and takes cover. Operation (106), the core event, is the closing beatitude - blessed are all who take refuge in him: trust named as the true end of the psalm's summons. Target (107) is refuge-taking itself (inferred): the aim is the sheltering, not any further object. Manner (108) is none - no mode is coloured; the blessing stands plainly. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are all absent: no degree is scored, nothing narrows the refuge, no downstream outcome is booked - the reading rests on the sheltering as a state. Coupling (112) is take-refuge: the affect is welded to the act of sheltering, feeling and flight to cover inseparable. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names the arc: from revolt the psalm lands here - the interior that stops fighting and shelters in the king is pronounced happy. Role (115) is characteristic - a standing trait, not a passing surge. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state: the refuge is a condition of the inner being, held within. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the whole self that has given up its rebellion takes cover in the king - a movement of trustful feeling welded to the act of sheltering, held wholly within as the blessed end-state the psalm drives toward.
narratives.story: This psalm has stormed with God's anger and human rebellion, kings and rulers set against the king God has installed. Then, at the very end, it turns and rests on a single quiet line: blessed are all who take refuge in him. After all the defiance, the happy person is the one who stops fighting and simply takes cover. It is a movement of the heart more than a calculated decision - a turning to shelter. The psalm does not say what finally makes a person do it; it just names the sheltering and calls it blessed. There is no strain in it and no reward tacked on beyond the shelter itself. It is the picture of someone who has laid down the struggle and found safety by hiding in the very king they might have fought - and is called happy for it.
narratives.variation_note: The item H2620:takerefug (chasah, 'take refuge') runs across fifteen distinct readings in this family; readings 1-10 are coded as affect held as an internal ib-state, and 11-15 shift toward action/disposition whose locus is external, in God. This first reading is the BEATITUDE that closes a psalm of revolt: refuge as the blessed end-state of those who abandon rebellion, the bearer generalised to 'all who trust,' held as an inner state.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'lie down and sleep in trust' - rest taken in the middle of mortal danger. Type (102) is state: a condition the self is in, not an act it performs. Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior spring; the verse credits the LORD's sustaining, but the row files no origin for the restfulness itself, resting on the fact of the sleep. Seat (104) resolves to none: the trust is not organ-located; the whole self, body and interior, lies down, not a faculty. Bearer (105) is the psalmist (inferred): the interior of the man surrounded by thousands who rise against him. Operation (106), the core event, is that the self lies down, sleeps, and wakes again - the sheer ability to surrender consciousness among enemies is trust made bodily. Target (107) is trustful-rest (inferred): the aim is the rest itself, sleep as the form the trust takes. Manner (108) is none - no mode is coloured; the sleeping is stated plainly. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no degree is scored, nothing narrows it, no downstream outcome is booked - the reading rests on the state of restful sleep. Coupling (112) is sleep-in-trust: the state is welded to the act of sleeping, the rest inseparable from the trust it embodies. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: the interior is so secure it can let go of consciousness among enemies - sleep itself the proof of trust. Role (115) is characteristic - a standing trait. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state: the trustful rest is a condition of the inner being that shows in the body. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the psalmist, ringed by thousands, lies down and sleeps and wakes - a whole self so secure it can surrender its own awareness, trust welded to sleep and lodged within as a bodily-shown state of rest, because the LORD sustains him.
narratives.story: On the run from his own son, with thousands of enemies closing in, the psalmist does something almost unthinkable: he goes to sleep. I lay down and slept, he says; I woke again, because the Lord kept me. In a situation built for sleepless terror, he simply rests. That ability to close his eyes and let go of consciousness while surrounded is itself the proof of his trust - fear would have kept him awake, but trust lets him sleep. The passage does not analyse how he manages it; it just reports the lying down, the sleeping, the waking. His trust here is not a speech or a resolve but something his whole body does. It is one of the most human pictures of faith in the Psalms: a hunted man who can still sleep through the night because he believes someone is keeping watch.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'trust in the LORD' - reliance placed where the offerings point. Type (102) is volition: this is an act of the will, a trust commanded and chosen, not a mere feeling. Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior spring; the call to trust simply follows the sacrifices, its origin unfiled. Seat (104) resolves to none: the trust is not organ-located; the whole hearer is directed to rely, not a faculty. Bearer (105) is the hearer (inferred): the interior of those addressed and told to offer and to trust. Operation (106), the core event, is that after right sacrifices the hearer is called to put trust in the LORD - reliance placed where the offerings were only pointing. Target (107) is entrustment (inferred): the aim is the handing-over of reliance to God. Manner (108) is none - no mode is coloured. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no degree, no narrowing, no booked outcome - the reading rests on the act of trusting. Coupling (112) is put-trust: the volition is welded to the act of entrusting, will and reliance one. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: the interior is directed past ritual to reliance - the sacrifices mean nothing without the trust. Role (115) is characteristic - a standing trait. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state: the trust is a condition of the inner being. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the hearer is told to offer right sacrifices and then, crucially, to put trust in the LORD - a willed reliance welded to the act of entrusting, lodged within as an inner state, the ritual carried through to its only real point, which is to rest the self on God.
narratives.story: This psalm is spoken to people who are restless and looking for something good, and it gives them a direction: offer right sacrifices, and put your trust in the Lord. The striking thing is the order and the emphasis - the ceremonies are not enough by themselves. They are only pointing somewhere, and the place they point is trust. The real thing being asked for is reliance on God, a deliberate handing-over of the self. It is something to be chosen and done, not just felt. The passage does not spell out where the trust comes from or what it yields; it simply moves the hearer past the ritual to the reliance the ritual was always about. It is the reminder that outward religion means little unless it lands in an inner leaning on God - that the point of it all is to actually trust him.
narratives.variation_note: Among the thirty-nine H0982:trust (batach) readings, this one is a COMMANDED trust (volition) directed to a general hearer and set past ritual - the sacrifices carried through to reliance - distinct from the psalmist's first-person trust or the descent-readings of trust in wealth, idols and princes.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'the joy of those who take refuge' - shelter blossoming into song. Type (102) is affect: a movement of glad feeling, not a bare deed. Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior spring; the joy simply rises within the refuge, its origin unfiled. Seat (104) resolves to none: the refuge is not organ-located; the whole self shelters and rejoices, not a faculty. Bearer (105) is 'those who take refuge' (inferred): the interior of the sheltering, set over against the rebellious enemies God will cast out. Operation (106), the core event, is that all who take refuge in God rejoice and ever sing for joy under his protection - shelter blossoming into song. Target (107) is refuge-joy (inferred): the aim is the gladness of the sheltered self. Manner (108) is none - no mode is coloured. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no degree, no narrowing, no booked outcome - the reading rests on the joy of the sheltered. Coupling (112) is refuge-and-sing: the affect is welded to song, the sheltering and the singing one movement. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names the contrast: over against the rebellious enemies, the interior of the sheltering is glad and vocal. Role (115) is characteristic - a standing trait. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state: the refuge-joy is a condition of the inner being. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, all who take cover in God do not merely survive but rejoice and sing without ceasing under his protection - the sheltering welded to gladness and song, held within as a bright inner state, the exact opposite of the destroyed rebels whose interior the psalm has just condemned.
narratives.story: This psalm has just described the destruction of God's enemies - liars, the bloodthirsty, the rebellious. Then it turns to the other side of the picture and shows what life inside God's shelter looks like: let all who take refuge in you rejoice; let them sing for joy forever. The people who take cover in God do not just barely survive; they are glad, and their gladness breaks out into song. Shelter here blossoms straight into music. The passage sets this bright, singing joy directly against the ruin of the wicked it has just pronounced. It does not explain where the joy comes from; it simply shows that being safe in God fills people with a happiness they cannot keep quiet. It is the picture of the sheltered life as not merely secure but joyful - people so at rest under God's protection that they sing.

This reading foregrounds refuge turning to JOY and SONG: the sheltered interior is not merely safe but glad and vocal, set against the destroyed rebels - refuge read on its bright affective side.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'depart from me, evildoers' - the sudden dismissal of the workers of evil. Type (102) is volition: an act of the will, a command issued, not a felt state. Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior spring; the turn simply happens, its origin unfiled. Seat (104) resolves to none: the dismissal is not organ-located; the whole self commands, not a faculty. Bearer (105) is the psalmist (inferred): the interior that has just been drenching its bed with tears and now rounds on its enemies. Operation (106), the core event, is the pivot itself - the self, now sure it is heard, dismisses the workers of evil: grief flipping to confident command. Target (107) is confident-dismissal (inferred): the aim is the expelling of the enemies. Manner (108) is none - no mode is coloured. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no degree, no narrowing, no booked outcome - the reading rests on the act of dismissal. Coupling (112) is depart-from-me: the volition is welded to the command of separation. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names the pivot: the same weeping that soaked the bed is now the proof God has heard, and the self turns to expel the enemies. Role (115) is characteristic - a standing trait. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state: the turn is a condition of the inner being. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the interior that had been dissolving in tears suddenly wheels about - certain now that the LORD has heard its weeping - and orders the workers of evil away: a willed dismissal welded to the command 'depart from me,' lodged within as the very moment grief becomes confidence.
narratives.story: For most of this psalm the writer is falling apart - languishing, groaning, flooding his bed with tears night after night. Then, without warning, everything turns. Depart from me, all you workers of evil, he says, for the Lord has heard the sound of my weeping. The very tears that had been the mark of his helplessness suddenly become the proof that God has heard him, and on the strength of that he rounds on his enemies and orders them away. It is a decision, a command he issues from a will that has just found its footing. The passage does not explain the shift; it simply catches the instant when despair flips into confidence. It is one of the most sudden turns in the Psalms - a broken man who, sure at last that he has been heard, straightens up and tells the evil around him to get out.
narratives.variation_note: The item H5493:depart (sur/'depart from me') has three readings: the self's command that evildoers leave it. This first reading is the PIVOT of a lament: grief flipping to confident command once the psalmist knows he is heard - a willed dismissal held as an inner state (internal:ib-state), distinct from the word-keeping separation of Psa 119:115 (external:person) and the aversive severance from bloodthirsty men in Psa 139:19.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'take refuge in you' - shelter sought first, before anything else. Type (102) is affect: a movement of reliant feeling, not a bare deed. Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior spring; the sheltering simply opens the psalm, its origin unfiled. Seat (104) resolves to none: the refuge is not organ-located; the whole self shelters, not a faculty. Bearer (105) is the psalmist (inferred): the interior of the one hunted by pursuers who would tear his soul like a lion. Operation (106), the core event, is that the self takes refuge in God and only then asks to be saved from all its pursuers - shelter sought first, the plea spoken from inside it. Target (107) is refuge-taking (inferred): the aim is the sheltering itself. Manner (108) is none - no mode is coloured. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no degree, no narrowing, no booked outcome - the reading rests on the sheltering. Coupling (112) is take-refuge: the affect is welded to the act of sheltering. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names the order: before the oath of innocence, the interior first shelters; the whole plea is spoken from inside that refuge. Role (115) is characteristic - a standing trait. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state: the refuge is a condition of the inner being. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the hunted self takes cover in God as its first move - a movement of reliant feeling welded to the act of sheltering, held within as an inner state, so that the appeal against the lion-like pursuers and the whole oath that follows are all uttered from within an already-taken refuge.
narratives.story: This psalm opens with a man being hunted, afraid of being torn apart like prey with no one to rescue him. But before he says anything about his danger, before he swears his innocence or calls for justice, he does one thing first: O Lord my God, in you I take refuge. He takes cover in God at the very start, and everything else he says is spoken from inside that shelter. The order matters - safety first, then the plea. It is a movement of the heart, a running to cover. The passage does not explain what prompts it; it simply shows the sheltering as his opening move. It is the instinct of someone in real danger who, before reaching for any other defence, ducks first into the one place he trusts, and only then looks out at the threat.

This reading foregrounds refuge as the FIRST MOVE: shelter taken before the oath and plea, so the whole psalm is spoken from inside an already-taken refuge - the bearer the hunted psalmist, held as an inner state.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'trust flows from knowing the name' - reliance grounded in acquaintance with God. Type (102) is affect: a reliant movement, not a bare deed. Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior spring behind the trust, though the verse itself supplies its ground in knowing the name; the row files the trust, not a separate origin. Seat (104) resolves to none: the trust is not organ-located; the whole self relies, not a faculty. Bearer (105) is 'those who know the name' (inferred): the interior of those acquainted with who God is. Operation (106), the core event, is that those who know God's name put their trust in him, for he has not forsaken those who seek him - knowledge grounding reliance. Target (107) is knowledge-grounded-trust (inferred): the aim is the reliance that rests on acquaintance. Manner (108) is none - no mode is coloured. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no degree, no narrowing, no booked outcome - the reading rests on the trust. Coupling (112) is know-name-trust: the affect is welded to the knowing, reliance inseparable from acquaintance. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: to know who God is, is to rely on him - trust tied to acquaintance. Role (115) is characteristic - a standing trait. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state: the trust is a condition of the inner being. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, those who have come to know God's name lean their weight on him - a reliant movement welded to that knowledge, held within as an inner state, grounded on the settled fact that he has never forsaken those who seek him: trust as the natural issue of knowing who God actually is.
narratives.story: In this psalm of thanksgiving, one line quietly explains where trust comes from: those who know your name put their trust in you, for you have not forsaken those who seek you. Trust here is not blind or arbitrary - it grows directly out of knowing who God is. The people who rely on him are the ones who have come to know his character, and their reliance is simply the natural result of that knowledge. Knowing and trusting are bound together; you lean on him because you know him. The passage backs it with a plain fact of experience: he has never abandoned those who look for him. It does not add anything further about how the trust feels or what it earns. It is the reassuring picture of confidence that rests on acquaintance - the more you actually know God, the more it makes sense to trust him.
narratives.variation_note: Among the batach readings, this one grounds trust in KNOWING GOD'S NAME - reliance as the issue of acquaintance, backed by God's record of not forsaking seekers - distinct from trust commanded (Psa 4:5) or trust chosen under fear (Psa 56:3).

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'take refuge, refuse to flee' - a trust that holds its ground. Type (102) is affect: a reliant movement, not a bare deed. Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior spring; the sheltering simply stands against the advisers' counsel, its origin unfiled. Seat (104) resolves to none: the refuge is not organ-located; the whole self shelters, not a faculty. Bearer (105) is the psalmist (inferred): the interior pressed by counsellors to flee like a bird to the mountain. Operation (106), the core event, is that in the LORD the self takes refuge and rejects the counsel to flee - trust that stays put while the wicked bend the bow. Target (107) is standing-trust (inferred): the aim is the refuge that does not run. Manner (108) is none - no mode is coloured. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no degree, no narrowing, no booked outcome - the reading rests on the standing refuge. Coupling (112) is refuse-to-flee: the affect is welded to the refusal of flight, sheltering and staying one movement. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names the contest: against the advisers' panic, the interior refuses flight and shelters in God. Role (115) is characteristic - a standing trait. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state: the standing refuge is a condition of the inner being. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the psalmist, urged to bolt for the hills while arrows are fitted to the string, instead takes cover in the LORD and stays - a reliant movement welded to the refusal to flee, held within as an inner state: refuge here is not escape but the courage to hold one's ground because the shelter is God, not a mountain.
narratives.story: The psalm opens with panicked advice: with the wicked already fitting arrows to the string, voices around the psalmist tell him to flee like a bird to the mountains. He answers them before they can finish: in the Lord I take refuge - how can you tell me to run? His refuge is not a place to escape to; it is a reason to stand still. Because he is sheltering in God, he does not need to bolt for the hills. Trust here shows itself precisely as not fleeing. The passage does not spell out his reasoning beyond that; it simply shows him holding his ground while everyone urges retreat. It is the picture of someone whose confidence in God gives him the nerve to stay put when panic says run - a shelter that steadies rather than a hiding place that flees.

This reading foregrounds refuge as STANDING GROUND: taken against advisers urging flight, it is the trust that refuses to run - shelter as steadiness rather than escape, held as an inner state.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'trust in steadfast love' - the deliberate turn onto God's covenant love. Type (102) is affect: a reliant movement of the inner being, not a bare deed. Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior spring; the turn simply happens against the churn, its origin unfiled. Seat (104) resolves to none: the trust is not organ-located; the whole self plants itself, not a faculty. Bearer (105) is the psalmist (inferred): the interior that has been taking counsel in itself and carrying sorrow in the heart all day. Operation (106), the core event, is that against the churn the self plants itself on God's steadfast love - the deliberate turn to trust. Target (107) is the-turn-to-trust (inferred): the aim is the turning itself, from deliberation to reliance. Manner (108) is none - no mode is coloured. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no degree, no narrowing, no booked outcome - the reading rests on the turn. Coupling (112) is trust-in-chesed: the affect is welded to God's covenant love as the thing leaned on. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names the hinge: the interior stops deliberating and rests its weight on God's covenant love. Role (115) is characteristic - a standing trait. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state: the trust is a condition of the inner being. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the self that has churned with self-counsel and daily sorrow makes a decisive turn - 'but I have trusted in your steadfast love' - planting its whole weight on God's chesed, a reliant movement welded to that covenant love and lodged within as the psalm's very hinge from anguish to rest.
narratives.story: This short psalm is almost all anguish - how long, how long, God seeming to forget, the enemy winning, the heart carrying sorrow all day long. The writer has been turning the problem over and over in his own mind and getting nowhere. Then comes the hinge, one small word that changes everything: but I have trusted in your steadfast love. He stops churning and sets his whole weight down on God's faithful love. Nothing in his circumstances has changed yet; what changes is where he rests. The passage does not explain how he makes the turn; it simply shows him making it, moving from restless self-counsel to a settled leaning on God. It is the picture of a person worn out by his own worrying who finally lays it down and chooses to trust - and finds, in that turn, the ground his heart was looking for.
narratives.variation_note: Among the batach readings, this one is the decisive TURN from churning self-counsel to reliance, leaned specifically on God's steadfast love (chesed) - the psalm's hinge from anguish to rest, distinct from trust as a settled disposition (Psa 84:12) or trust chosen inside fear (Psa 56:3).

Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior spring; the sheltering simply opens the psalm, its origin unfiled. Seat (104) resolves to none: the refuge is not organ-located; the whole self shelters, not a faculty. Bearer (105) is the psalmist (inferred): the interior that has no good apart from God. Operation (106), the core event, is that the self takes refuge in God as the ground of its preservation - shelter as the opening posture from which all the psalm's contentment is spoken. Target (107) is refuge-taking (inferred): the aim is the sheltering itself. Manner (108) is none - no mode is coloured. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no degree, no narrowing, no booked outcome - the reading rests on the sheltering. Coupling (112) is take-refuge: the affect is welded to the act of sheltering. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: trust is the starting point, not a conclusion - the whole psalm's contentment is spoken from inside this refuge. Role (115) is characteristic - a standing trait. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state: the refuge is a condition of the inner being. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the self that reckons it has no good apart from God takes cover in him at the very outset - a reliant movement welded to the act of sheltering, held within as an inner state, the ground from which the psalm's whole song of a beautiful inheritance, a glad heart, and secure flesh then flows.
narratives.story: This psalm is full of contentment - a beautiful inheritance, pleasant places, a glad heart, a body that rests secure. But all of that rests on one thing said in the very first line: preserve me, O God, for in you I take refuge. The sheltering comes first, and everything settled and happy that follows is spoken from inside it. Taking cover in God is not where the psalm arrives at the end; it is where it starts. The passage does not explain what drives the writer to it; it simply makes the refuge the foundation of the whole song. It is the picture of a person whose deep peace and satisfaction are not free-floating but grounded - who can speak of having no lack precisely because, before anything else, he has hidden himself in God and knows he has no good apart from him.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'take refuge in the rock' - shelter in a cluster of strongholds. Type (102) is affect: a reliant movement, not a bare deed. Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior spring; the sheltering simply stands as the posture from which the rescue is told, its origin unfiled. Seat (104) resolves to none: the refuge is not organ-located; the whole self shelters, not a faculty. Bearer (105) is the psalmist (inferred): the interior of the delivered servant who loves the LORD his strength. Operation (106), the core event, is that the self takes refuge in God named as rock, fortress, shield, horn of salvation, stronghold - shelter piled under a heap of fortress-images. Target (107) is refuge-taking (inferred): the aim is the sheltering itself. Manner (108) is none - no mode is coloured. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no degree, no narrowing, no booked outcome - the reading rests on the sheltering. Coupling (112) is take-refuge: the affect is welded to the act of sheltering. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: the interior shelters in God under a pile of fortress-images; refuge is the posture from which the whole rescue is recounted. Role (115) is characteristic - a standing trait. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state: the refuge is a condition of the inner being. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the delivered servant takes cover in God - rock, fortress, shield, horn, stronghold all at once - a reliant movement welded to the act of sheltering and held within as an inner state, the settled posture from which the great storm-and-rescue that follows is sung.
narratives.story: This psalm of a rescued king opens by piling up names for God like a wall of stone: my rock, my fortress, my deliverer, my shield, the horn of my salvation, my stronghold - my God, in whom I take refuge. The sheer stack of fortress-images shows how completely the writer has taken cover. Before he tells the story of his rescue - the earth shaking, God coming down in fire and storm - he first plants himself inside this shelter, and the whole dramatic account is told from within it. The passage does not analyse the impulse; it simply shows a man who has found God to be every kind of stronghold at once and has hidden himself in all of them. It is the picture of someone so sure of where his safety lies that he can hardly find enough words for it, sheltering in a God who is rock and fortress and shield together.
narratives.variation_note: The item H2620:takerefug (chasah, 'take refuge') runs across fifteen distinct readings in this family; readings 1-10 are coded as affect held as an internal ib-state, and 11-15 shift toward action/disposition whose locus is external, in God. This reading foregrounds refuge under a CLUSTER OF STRONGHOLD-IMAGES (rock, fortress, shield, horn): the delivered king's sheltering is the posture from which the whole storm-and-rescue narrative is sung, held as an inner state.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'trust the name, not chariots' (zakar, here rendered trust) - reliance deliberately relocated from military might to God. Type (102) is affect: a reliant movement, not a bare deed. Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior spring; the relocation of confidence simply stands, its origin unfiled. narratives.story: On the eve of battle this psalm draws a plain contrast. Some people, it says, trust in chariots and some in horses - in the hardware of war, the strongest thing they can see. But we trust in the name of the Lord our God. The confidence is deliberately moved from military might to God himself. It is a choice about where to rest, made out loud and set against the obvious alternative. And the psalm follows it to its result: those who trust in chariots collapse and fall, while those who trust in God rise and stand upright. The passage does not explain the reasoning further; it simply lets the two reliances stand side by side and names the winner. It is the picture of a people refusing to pin their security on the visible, countable strength everyone else leans on, and fixing it instead on the name of their God.

Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no degree, no narrowing, no booked outcome - though the verse ties immovability to the trust, that stability is read through the coupling, not filed as a separate effect. narratives.story: This is a psalm about a king who has been given everything - a crown of gold, long life, glory, the joy of God's presence. But the psalm locates the real secret of his security in one line: the king trusts in the Lord, and through the steadfast love of the Most High he will not be moved. All the blessings sit on top of that trust. What keeps him steady is not his crown or his victories but his reliance on God, and the passage ties the two together directly: because he trusts, he cannot be shaken. It does not explain the trust further; it simply shows that the king's immovability grows straight out of it. It is the picture of a powerful man whose stability comes not from his own strength but from where he has chosen to lean - and who stands unshaken because that place is God.
narratives.variation_note: Among the batach readings, this one is read for its OUTCOME - trust that makes the bearer (a king) immovable through God's steadfast love - stability grown directly from reliance, distinct from trust as a bare turn (Psa 13:5) or a summons (Psa 115).

narratives.story: This is the psalm that begins in utter abandonment - my God, my God, why have you forsaken me? - a man crying out day and night with no answer. And in the middle of that silence he reaches back into history for something to hold onto: in you our fathers trusted; they trusted, and you delivered them. He remembers that his ancestors leaned on God and were rescued, not put to shame. It is trust borrowed from the past to steady a present that feels empty of God. He cannot feel the rescue himself yet, so he holds up the memory of theirs as evidence that God is the kind of God who comes through. The passage does not resolve his anguish here; it simply shows him gripping the ancestors' experience as an anchor. It is the very human act of clinging to what God has done for others when you cannot see him doing it for you.
narratives.variation_note: Among the batach readings, this one places trust in the FATHERS (a remembered, ancestral bearer) and is invoked from inside present dereliction as an anchor - trust recalled from the past against God's felt silence, distinct from the psalmist's own first-person trust elsewhere.

narratives.story: Surrounded by mockers who sneer that God will not save him, the psalmist answers by reaching back further than any of them can see - all the way to his own infancy. It was you, he tells God, who took me from the womb; you made me trust you even at my mother's breast. His reliance on God is not something he took up recently; it is older than his own memory, laid down before he could think or choose. He has been leaning on God since he was a baby. So when he pleads for help now, he is not appealing on the strength of a passing decision but on the strength of a lifelong bond. The passage does not argue it further; it simply grounds the whole prayer in a trust as old as his life. It is the picture of someone whose faith runs so deep it reaches back before he can remember not having it.
narratives.variation_note: Among the batach readings, this one grounds trust in INFANCY - a reliance God himself made at the breast, older than memory - the psalmist's plea resting on a lifelong bond rather than a recent turn (contrast Psa 13:5) or a summons (Psa 115).

Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no degree, no narrowing, no booked outcome - the reading rests on the trust. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the psalmist lifts his soul to God and leans his weight there - 'in you I trust' - even as the fear of being shamed and of enemies gloating presses hard; a reliant movement welded to that dread and held within as an inner state, trust exercised not in calm but exactly where humiliation threatens.
narratives.story: The psalm opens with the writer lifting his whole self up to God - to you I lift up my soul - and immediately naming what he is afraid of: being put to shame, having his enemies gloat over him. Right there, in the pressure of that fear, he says: O my God, in you I trust. His trust is not a calm, untroubled thing; it is held tight against the very real danger of humiliation. He leans on God precisely where he feels most exposed. The passage keeps the trust and the vulnerability side by side, not pretending the threat is gone. It does not explain the trust further; it simply shows him relying on God in the middle of his fear. It is the honest picture of faith not as the absence of dread but as leaning on God exactly when shame and defeat feel closest.
narratives.variation_note: Among the batach readings, this one holds trust and VULNERABILITY together - reliance exercised under the pressing threat of shame and gloating enemies - faith in the danger rather than after it, distinct from the settled disposition of Psa 84:12.

Seat (104) resolves to none: the refuge is not organ-located; the whole self shelters, not a faculty. narratives.story: Near the end of a long, aching prayer - the writer lonely, afflicted, hated with violent hatred - he asks God to guard his life and rescue him and keep him from shame. And he gives a reason for expecting to be heard: for I take refuge in you. The sheltering is not just one more request; it is the ground the whole plea stands on. Because he has hidden himself in God, he can ask God to protect him and mean it. His refuge is the reason he believes the prayer will land. The passage does not explain it beyond that; it simply makes the taking of cover the basis of the appeal. It is the picture of a worn-down, friendless person who has nowhere else to turn, and who leans on the one fact that he has turned to God - and rests his whole hope on that.
narratives.variation_note: The item H2620:takerefug (chasah, 'take refuge') runs across fifteen distinct readings in this family; readings 1-10 are coded as affect held as an internal ib-state, and 11-15 shift toward action/disposition whose locus is external, in God. This reading makes refuge the GROUND OF THE PLEA: the lonely, hated psalmist asks to be guarded and not shamed precisely because he takes refuge in God - shelter offered as the reason the prayer expects a hearing, held as an inner state.

Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior spring; the steady trust simply stands as part of the psalmist's integrity, its origin unfiled. Seat (104) resolves to none: the trust is not organ-located; the whole self relies, not a faculty. Bearer (105) is the psalmist (inferred): the interior of the one asking to be vindicated for his integrity. Operation (106), the core event, is that the self has trusted in the LORD without wavering or slipping - steady reliance offered as part of the integrity he stakes his vindication on. Target (107) is unwavering-trust (inferred): the aim is the reliance that does not sag. Manner (108) is none - no mode is coloured, though 'without wavering' colours the sense. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no degree, no narrowing, no booked outcome - the reading rests on the steady trust. Coupling (112) is trust-not-waver: the affect is welded to its own steadiness, reliance and constancy one. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names the distinction: distinct from the outward walk, the interior's reliance has not slipped or sagged - a constancy of trust. Role (115) is characteristic - a standing trait. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state: the trust is a condition of the inner being. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the psalmist offers as evidence for his vindication not only a blameless walk but a reliance that has held firm without wavering - a reliant movement welded to its own steadiness and held within as an inner state, trust weighed here not by its object alone but by its constancy: it has not slipped.
narratives.story: Asking God to vindicate him, the psalmist points to two things: I have walked in my integrity, and I have trusted in the Lord without wavering. The second is as important as the first. It is not only that he has behaved well outwardly, but that his reliance on God has held steady on the inside - it has not slipped, sagged, or drifted. He offers the constancy of his trust as part of the case for his innocence. What is being weighed here is not just where his trust is aimed but how firmly it has held. The passage does not elaborate; it simply names a reliance that has stayed put. It is the picture of someone whose faith is not a fair-weather thing but a settled steadiness he can point to - a trust that has kept its grip through everything and never let go.
narratives.variation_note: Among the batach readings, this one is weighed by its CONSTANCY - trust that has held 'without wavering,' offered as part of the psalmist's integrity - reliance measured by its steadiness rather than its object, distinct from a single decisive turn (Psa 13:5).

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'my heart trusts and is helped' - reliance met by God's aid. Type (102) is affect: a reliant movement, not a bare deed. Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior spring; the trust simply rests on the LORD as strength and shield, its origin unfiled. Seat (104) resolves to none: though 'heart' is named, the operation is not treated as organ-lodged - 'heart' reads as the whole inner person trusting, not a faculty switched on. Bearer (105) is the psalmist (inferred): the interior that had feared going down to the pit and now blesses God for hearing. Operation (106), the core event, is that the LORD is the self's strength and shield; in him the heart trusts and is helped - trust answered by help. Target (107) is trust-answered (inferred): the aim is the reliance that meets God's aid. Manner (108) is none - no mode is coloured. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no degree, no narrowing, no booked outcome - though help follows the trust, it is read through the coupling, not filed as a separate effect. Coupling (112) is heart-trusts-helped: the affect is welded to the help it meets, reliance and rescue joined. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: the heart's reliance meeting God's aid - trust and rescue joined. Role (115) is characteristic - a standing trait. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state: the trust is a condition of the inner being. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the psalmist who dreaded the pit finds the LORD his strength and shield, and his heart, leaning there, is helped - a reliant movement welded to the help that answers it, held within as an inner state that overflows into exultation and song: trust here shown at the moment it is met, reliance and aid meeting so that the heart breaks into thanks.
narratives.story: Earlier in this psalm the writer feared he would sink like those who go down to the pit. By verse seven everything has lifted: the Lord is my strength and my shield; in him my heart trusts, and I am helped. The trust and the help arrive together - he leans on God with his whole heart, and he is answered. And the relief overflows: his heart leaps, and he breaks into song and thanks. What the passage shows is the moment reliance meets rescue, the instant trusting turns into being helped. It does not separate the two or explain the mechanism; it simply lets them meet and lets the joy follow. It is the picture of a person who cast his weight on God in real fear and felt God take it - and could not help but sing about it afterward.
narratives.variation_note: Among the batach readings, this one is trust CAUGHT AT THE MOMENT IT IS MET - the heart's reliance answered by help and overflowing into song - reliance and rescue joined, distinct from trust invoked in ongoing danger (Psa 25:2).

Seat (104) resolves to none: the refuge is not organ-located; the whole self shelters, not a faculty. Bearer (105) is the psalmist (inferred): the interior of the besieged one who will commit his spirit into God's hand. Operation (106), the core event, is that the self takes refuge in God, asking never to be put to shame and to be delivered in his righteousness - shelter as the posture the whole plea is spoken from. Target (107) is refuge-taking (inferred): the aim is the sheltering itself. Manner (108) is none - no mode is coloured. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no degree, no narrowing, no booked outcome - the reading rests on the sheltering. Coupling (112) is take-refuge: the affect is welded to the act of sheltering. Prohibition (113) is absent. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the besieged psalmist takes cover in God at the outset - 'in you, O LORD, do I take refuge; let me never be put to shame' - a reliant movement welded to the act of sheltering and held within as an inner state, the ground from which the long psalm's committing of the spirit, its terror on every side, and its final trust all proceed.
narratives.story: This long psalm runs through terror on every side, whispering enemies, a body wasted with grief, a life spent with sorrow. But it opens by planting itself somewhere safe: in you, O Lord, I take refuge; let me never be put to shame. The sheltering is the first move, and everything that follows - handing his spirit into God's hand, naming God as his rock and fortress, and at last declaring his trust - is spoken from inside that refuge. The passage does not explain the impulse; it simply makes the taking of cover the starting posture of the whole prayer. It is the picture of a person under siege who, before he pours out any of his distress, first steps into the one shelter he trusts, and speaks the rest of his fear and hope from within its walls.
narratives.variation_note: The item H2620:takerefug (chasah, 'take refuge') runs across fifteen distinct readings in this family; readings 1-10 are coded as affect held as an internal ib-state, and 11-15 shift toward action/disposition whose locus is external, in God. This reading is refuge as OPENING POSTURE of a long lament: shelter taken at the outset so the whole psalm - committing the spirit, terror on every side, final trust - is spoken from inside it, held as an inner state. It shares Psa 31 with two batach readings (v6, v14).

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'my times are in your hand' - the whole course of life entrusted. Type (102) is affect: a reliant movement, not a bare deed. Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior spring; the turn to trust simply rises against the terror, its origin unfiled. Seat (104) resolves to none: the trust is not organ-located; the whole self entrusts, not a faculty. Bearer (105) is the psalmist (inferred): the interior ringed by scheming enemies and 'terror on every side.' Operation (106), the core event, is that against the terror the self trusts, saying 'you are my God; my times are in your hand' - the whole course of life handed over. Target (107) is entrusting-my-times (inferred): the aim is the surrender of one's whole timing to God. Manner (108) is none - no mode is coloured. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no degree, no narrowing, no booked outcome - the reading rests on the entrusting. Coupling (112) is times-in-your-hand: the affect is welded to that surrender, trust and the handing-over of life's timing one. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names the turn: from dread to trust - the interior hands over not just its spirit but the timing of its whole life. Role (115) is characteristic - a standing trait. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state: the trust is a condition of the inner being. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the psalmist, hearing the plots to take his life, turns and lays his whole life in God's hand - 'but I trust in you... my times are in your hand' - a reliant movement welded to that total surrender and held within as an inner state: trust here reaches its widest, giving over not a moment but the entire span and timing of one's days.
narratives.story: Hemmed in by enemies plotting to take his life, with terror on every side, the psalmist makes a decisive turn: but I trust in you, O Lord; I say, You are my God. My times are in your hand. It is not a small trust for a single crisis - he hands over the whole timing of his life, every day still to come, into God's keeping. Whatever happens and whenever it happens, it is God's to hold. The trust reaches as wide as trust can reach. The passage does not soften the danger or explain the turn; it simply shows a threatened man giving over not just this moment but his entire future. It is the picture of someone who, unable to control what will become of him, lays the whole span of his days in God's hands and rests there.
narratives.variation_note: Among the batach readings, this one reaches WIDEST - the surrender of one's whole life and timing ('my times are in your hand') against terror on every side - total entrustment, distinct from a trust aimed at a single rescue (Psa 28:7). It shares Psa 31 with v6 and the refuge of v1.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'I trust in the LORD, not idols' - reliance fixed on God against emptiness. Type (102) is affect: a reliant movement, not a bare deed. Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior spring; the trust simply stands over against the idols, its origin unfiled. Seat (104) resolves to none: the trust is not organ-located; the whole self relies, not a faculty. Bearer (105) is the psalmist (inferred): the interior that hates those who cling to worthless idols. Operation (106), the core event, is that the self hates those who pay regard to worthless idols and trusts instead in the LORD - reliance fixed on God against emptiness. Target (107) is idol-refusing-trust (inferred): the aim is the reliance that rejects the empty gods. Manner (108) is none - no mode is coloured. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no degree, no narrowing, no booked outcome - the reading rests on the trust. Coupling (112) is trust-not-idols: the affect is welded to the refusal of idols, reliance defined against what it rejects. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names the contrast: two directions of reliance - the interior refuses the empty gods and rests on God. Role (115) is characteristic - a standing trait. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state: the trust is a condition of the inner being. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the psalmist sets his reliance by rejecting its counterfeit - hating those who cling to worthless idols and trusting the LORD instead - a reliant movement welded to that refusal and held within as an inner state: trust here defined by its opposite, a confidence that knows itself precisely because it has turned its back on the empty things others lean on.
narratives.story: In the middle of this psalm the writer draws a sharp line between himself and other people by pointing at what they lean on. He hates, he says, those who cling to worthless idols - but I trust in the Lord. His trust defines itself against its counterfeit: he knows what he relies on partly by knowing what he refuses. Others put their weight on empty, lifeless things; he puts his on the living God. The passage does not argue the point; it simply sets the two directions of reliance side by side and plants the psalmist firmly on one of them. It is the picture of a person whose faith is clear-eyed about the alternatives - who has looked at the empty things people trust and turned deliberately away from them to rest on God alone.
narratives.variation_note: Among the batach readings, this one is DEFINED BY CONTRAST - trust fixed on the LORD precisely by rejecting worthless idols - reliance known by what it refuses, an ascent-reading set against the idol-trust of the descent-readings (Psa 115:8; 135:18). It shares Psa 31 with v14 and the refuge of v1.

Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior spring; the trust simply stands, its origin unfiled. Seat (104) resolves to none: the trust is not organ-located; the whole self relies, not a faculty. Bearer (105) is 'the one who trusts' (inferred): the interior encircled by God's steadfast love, set against the wicked and their many sorrows. Operation (106), the core event, is that many are the sorrows of the wicked, but steadfast love surrounds the one who trusts in the LORD - trust encircled by love. Target (107) is encircling-love (inferred): the aim, and the surrounding, is God's chesed around the truster. Manner (108) is none - no mode is coloured. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no degree, no narrowing, no booked outcome - the encircling is read through the coupling, not filed as a separate effect. Coupling (112) is trust-surrounded: the affect is welded to the ring of love around it, reliance and its encirclement one. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: the operation sets the trusting interior inside a ring of love, over against the wicked's many sorrows. Role (115) is characteristic - a standing trait. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state: the trust is a condition of the inner being. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the one who leans on the LORD is set inside an encircling of steadfast love - a reliant movement welded to the ring of chesed around it, held within as an inner state and drawn in deliberate contrast to the wicked, whose interior is ringed instead by many sorrows: trust here read for the environment it creates, a self surrounded by love because it relies.
narratives.story: This psalm of forgiveness ends with a plain contrast about the two kinds of inner life. Many are the sorrows of the wicked, it says, but steadfast love surrounds the one who trusts in the Lord. The person who leans on God is pictured as ringed round by God's faithful love - it encircles him. The wicked, by contrast, are surrounded by their own griefs. What trust does here is create an environment: it sets the truster inside a circle of love. The passage does not explain the mechanism; it simply draws the two pictures side by side and lets them stand. It is the reassuring image of what it feels like to rely on God - not that troubles vanish, but that the trusting person is wrapped around by a love that holds him, while those who refuse are left encircled by sorrow instead.
narratives.variation_note: Among the batach readings, this one is read for the ENVIRONMENT it creates - the truster ringed round by steadfast love, set against the wicked ringed by sorrow - trust seen in what surrounds it, distinct from trust as an inward turn (Psa 13:5).

Seat (104) resolves to none: the refuge is not organ-located; the whole self shelters, not a faculty. Bearer (105) is 'those who take refuge' (inferred): the interior of God's servants whose life he redeems. Operation (106), the core event, is that the LORD redeems the life of his servants; none who take refuge in him will be condemned - shelter that guarantees acquittal. Target (107) is refuge-taking (inferred): the aim is the sheltering itself. Manner (108) is none - no mode is coloured. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no degree, no narrowing, no booked outcome - the guarantee of acquittal is read through the coupling, not filed as a separate effect. Coupling (112) is refuge-not-condemned: the affect is welded to the safety from condemnation, sheltering and acquittal one. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: the operation closes the acrostic on refuge - the interior that shelters in God is safe from condemnation. Role (115) is characteristic - a standing trait. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state: the refuge is a condition of the inner being. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the whole acrostic psalm of God's care for the afflicted lands on its last note - the LORD redeems his servants, and none who take cover in him will be condemned - a reliant movement welded to that guaranteed acquittal and held within as an inner state: refuge read for its outcome, the settled safety of the sheltered self from all condemnation.
narratives.story: This long alphabet psalm, full of God's care for the afflicted and the brokenhearted, saves its final word for the people who take shelter in him: the Lord redeems the life of his servants; none of those who take refuge in him will be condemned. The sheltering carries a guarantee - those who hide in God are safe not just from present trouble but from condemnation itself. The whole psalm has been building toward this settled assurance. The passage does not spell out the mechanism; it simply closes on the safety of the sheltered. It is the picture of refuge that reaches all the way to the final verdict - the confidence that a person who has taken cover in God will never, in the end, be counted guilty and cast off. Trust here ends in acquittal.
narratives.variation_note: The item H2620:takerefug (chasah, 'take refuge') runs across fifteen distinct readings in this family; readings 1-10 are coded as affect held as an internal ib-state, and 11-15 shift toward action/disposition whose locus is external, in God. This reading closes an acrostic on refuge read for its OUTCOME - the sheltered self guaranteed acquittal, 'none will be condemned' - safety reaching to the final verdict, held as an inner state. Psa 34 also holds the taste-reading (v8).

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is 'taste and see that the LORD is good' - trust made experiential, savoured. Type (102) is affect: a movement of felt experience, not a bare deed.
