Manner (108) is none - no mode is coloured. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no degree, no narrowing, no booked outcome. Coupling (112) here carries the value 'external:god' - the refuge is registered as welded to God, its binding pointing wholly outside the self. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: reliance on God preferred to reliance on the powerful. Role (115) is characteristic - a standing trait. Locus (116) here is recorded as 'paired with the folly of trusting princes' - the refuge is set against the lesser trust in princes it is compared to. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the psalmist repeats his settled preference against the highest human power - it is better to take refuge in the LORD than to trust in princes - a sheltering whose binding points wholly outside the self to God, paired against the folly of leaning on the mighty: refuge here is chosen over even the strongest human security, the shelter in God named the better ground no matter how impressive the alternative.
narratives.story: The bright side of the sharper comparison: it is better to take refuge in the Lord than to trust in princes. Set against the mightiest human help there is - rulers with real power to act - the psalmist still names sheltering in God the better choice. His preference does not waver even when the alternative is at its most impressive. It is a settled conviction, pointed wholly at God: whatever strength princes command, hiding in God is wiser. The passage sets refuge in God directly against reliance on the powerful and comes down, again, firmly on the refuge. It is the steady wisdom of a person who is not dazzled by human greatness - who has seen that even the strongest rulers can fail, and that the surest place to put your weight, always, is God.
narratives.variation_note: The item H2620:takerefug (chasah, 'take refuge') runs across fifteen distinct readings in this family; readings 1-10 are coded as affect held as an internal ib-state, and 11-15 shift toward action/disposition whose locus is external, in God. This fifteenth reading (chasah, disposition, external:god) closes the item on refuge ranked above the MIGHTIEST human ground - 'better than to trust in princes' - a settled preference paired against its descent-counterpart trust-in-princes (trust#34), the sharper twin of the v8 comparison.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is batach - 'for I trust in your word' - reliance on God's word as the ground of an answer to the taunter. Type (102) is disposition: a settled bearing of the psalmist toward God's word. Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior spring; the trust simply stands, its origin unfiled. Seat (104) resolves to none: the trust is not organ-located; the whole self relies, not a faculty. Bearer (105) is the psalmist (inferred): the interior taunted by the insolent, armed by God's word. Operation (106), the core event, is trust - reliance placed on God's word. Target (107) is God's word (inferred): the reliance is aimed at the word, not directly at a rescue. Manner (108) is none - no mode is coloured. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no degree, no narrowing, no booked outcome. Coupling (112) is paired within its char-arc across the psalm (inferred): the trust is welded to the wider run of the psalmist's devotion to the word through Psalm 119. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: trust in the word that arms him against the taunter - reliance on God's promise as his answer. Role (115) is characteristic - a standing trait. Locus (116) is external:god - the reference-point is set outside the self, in God (his word). The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the taunted psalmist finds his answer in a settled reliance on God's word - 'then shall I have an answer for him who taunts me, for I trust in your word' - a disposition welded to his lifelong devotion to the word and located external:god: here trust fixes not on a rescue but on God's promise itself, the word so relied upon that it becomes the very reply he can give to mockery, confidence in what God has said standing as his defence.
narratives.story: In the long psalm devoted to God's law, the writer names what lets him face those who mock him: then shall I have an answer for him who taunts me, for I trust in your word. His trust here fixes on something specific - God's word, his promise. Because he relies on what God has said, he has a reply ready for the insolent who deride him. The reliance is a settled bearing that runs all through this psalm's love of the word, and it points entirely at God. The passage does not aim the trust at a rescue so much as at the promise itself: he leans his whole weight on what God has spoken, and that becomes his defence. It is the picture of a person armed against ridicule not by clever comebacks but by confidence in God's word - so sure of the promise that it steadies him against every taunt.
narratives.variation_note: Among the batach readings, this one fixes trust on GOD'S WORD - reliance on the promise itself as an answer to the taunter (external:god) - the object is the word rather than a rescue, distinct from trust aimed at deliverance (Psa 28:7) or at God's steadfast love (Psa 52:8).

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is sur - 'depart from me, you evildoers' - the separation from evildoers the psalmist enacts to keep the word. Type (102) is action: a doing, a putting-away, not a mere feeling. Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior spring; the separation simply stands, its origin unfiled. Seat (104) resolves to none: the putting-away is not organ-located; the whole self acts, not a faculty. Bearer (105) is the psalmist (inferred): the interior that hates the double-minded and loves God's law. Operation (106), the core event, is to put the evildoers away - drawing a line so that he may keep the commandments of his God. Target (107) is the psalmist (inferred): the separation serves his own keeping of the word, clearing his space of their interference. Manner (108) is none - no mode is coloured. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no degree, no narrowing, no booked outcome. Coupling (112) is paired within its char-arc across the psalm (inferred): the putting-away is welded to the wider run of the psalmist's devotion to the word. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: the separation from evildoers the psalmist enacts to keep the word - clearing them off so he can obey. Role (115) is characteristic - a standing trait. Locus (116) is external:person - and this is the distinctive finding: unlike the inner-state dismissals elsewhere, the reference-point here is set toward other persons, the evildoers put at a distance. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the psalmist orders the evildoers away for a stated purpose - 'that I may keep the commandments of my God' - an act of separation whose reference-point is set outside the self toward persons: here the command 'depart' is not a burst of confidence but a deliberate clearing of company, the interior fencing off the wicked so that its devotion to God's word can go unhindered, distance from evil people made a condition of obedience.
narratives.story: In the middle of his devotion to God's law, the psalmist turns and orders the wrong company away: depart from me, you evildoers, that I may keep the commandments of my God. This is not a triumphant dismissal of enemies but a deliberate clearing of his space. He wants to obey God, and he recognises that the wrong people around him get in the way of that, so he puts them at a distance. Separation from evildoers becomes, for him, a condition of keeping the word. The passage ties the two together plainly: get away from me, so that I can follow God. It is the practical picture of someone serious about obedience who understands that whom you keep company with matters - and who is willing to draw a hard line around the wicked in order to protect his own faithfulness to God.
narratives.variation_note: See the variation note at Psa 6:8 (H5493:depart#1). This second reading is a deliberate SEPARATION-FOR-OBEDIENCE - the evildoers put away 'that I may keep the commandments' - the one depart-reading located external:person (an action toward others), distinct from the confident lament-pivot of Psa 6:8 and the aversive severance of Psa 139:19, both held as inner states.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is shaanan - 'the scorn of those who are at ease' - the complacency whose comfort breeds contempt for the afflicted. Type (102) is status: not a single act but a settled condition of the comfortable, ease as their standing state. Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior spring; the complacency simply stands, its origin unfiled. Seat (104) resolves to none: the ease is not organ-located; the whole self of the comfortable is at ease, not a faculty. Bearer (105) is the complacent (inferred): the interior of the proud and comfortable who scorn. Operation (106), the core event, is to be at ease - a settled comfort that turns to contempt. Target (107) is 'scorning the afflicted' (inferred): the ease aims its scorn at the afflicted. Manner (108) is none - no mode is coloured. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no degree, no narrowing, no booked outcome. Coupling (112) here carries the value 'internal:ib-state' - the ease is registered as bound to the inner condition, comfort and contempt held together. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: the complacent, whose comfortable ease breeds contempt for the afflicted. Role (115) is characteristic - a standing trait of the complacent. Locus (116) here is recorded as 'paired with the proud' - the ease is set alongside the pride it keeps company with. The full process, read at full weight in its descent: from no named source and no organ-seat, the comfortable are settled in an ease that has curdled into scorn - heaping contempt on the afflicted from the safety of their own untroubled lives - a status bound to an inner condition and paired with pride: here the family's security is read on its shadow side, not the shelter of the trusting but the complacency of the comfortable, an ease so undisturbed that it looks down on those who suffer, the smugness that has never had to take refuge and so despises those who must.
narratives.story: This short psalm is prayed by people who have had more than enough of being looked down on - worn out, as they say, by the scorn of those who are at ease and the contempt of the proud. It puts a name to a particular kind of person: the comfortable, the ones whose lives are settled and untroubled, and whose very ease has curdled into contempt for those who suffer. Their comfort has made them cruel; safe themselves, they sneer at the afflicted. It is a settled condition, not a passing mood, and it keeps company with pride. The passage reads this smug ease at full weight and sets the humble, upward-looking prayer of the oppressed against it. It is the uncomfortable picture of complacency - people so cushioned by their own security that they have grown scornful of anyone who has to struggle, the flip side of a trust they have never needed.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is batach - 'those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion' - reliance that grounds the self into immovability. Type (102) is disposition: a settled bearing that produces stability. Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior spring; the trust simply stands, its origin unfiled. Seat (104) resolves to none: the trust is not organ-located; the whole self relies, not a faculty. Bearer (105) is 'those who trust' (inferred): the collective interior likened to the unmovable mountain. Operation (106), the core event, is to ground the self in God - reliance that makes the truster immovable. Target (107) is 'so as to be immovable' (inferred): the aim, and the result, is the immovability of a mountain. Manner (108) is none - no mode is coloured. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no degree, no narrowing, no booked outcome. Coupling (112) here carries the value 'internal:ib-state' - the trust is registered as bound to the inner condition. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: the operation of trust grounding the self - reliance on God produces the immovability of a mountain. Role (115) is characteristic - a standing trait. Locus (116) here is recorded as 'paired with the abiding-forever stability' - the trust is set alongside the abiding, unshaken permanence of Zion. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, those who trust in the LORD are grounded like Mount Zion, which cannot be moved but abides forever - a settled disposition bound to an inner condition and paired with that abiding stability: here trust is read for what it does to the truster's footing, reliance so anchoring that it makes the person as unshakeable and permanent as a mountain, the inner self given the fixedness of Zion by the simple act of leaning on God.
narratives.story: This song of ascents opens with a picture of what trust does to a person: those who trust in the Lord are like Mount Zion, which cannot be moved, but abides forever. Reliance on God gives the truster the fixedness of a mountain - unshaken, permanent, immovable. The trust is a settled bearing, and it grounds the whole self so firmly that no pressure can topple it. The passage does not analyse the trust; it simply likens the trusting person to Zion and lets the image do the work. It is the steadying picture of faith as an anchor - not that the trusting escape all trouble, but that they cannot be dislodged, standing as solid and lasting as the mountain of God himself. To lean on God, the psalm says, is to become unmovable.
narratives.variation_note: Among the batach readings, this one is read for the FOOTING it gives - the truster made immovable as Mount Zion, abiding forever (internal:ib-state) - reliance seen in the mountain-like fixedness it produces, kin to Psa 21:7 (unmoved) and Psa 112:7 (firm heart) but imaged here as permanence.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is batach - 'so do all who trust in them' - the misplaced trust that shares the idol's deadness. Type (102) is disposition: a settled bearing, here bent toward lifeless things. Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior spring; the misplaced trust simply stands, its origin unfiled. Seat (104) resolves to none: the trust is not organ-located; the whole self of the idolater relies, not a faculty. Bearer (105) is the idolaters (inferred): the interior of those who make and trust idols. Operation (106), the core event, is trust - reliance fixed on dead idols. Target (107) is 'in dead idols' (inferred): the reliance is aimed at lifeless images. Manner (108) is none - no mode is coloured. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no degree, no narrowing, no booked outcome. Coupling (112) here carries the value 'internal:ib-state' - the misplaced trust is registered as bound to the inner condition, reliance and the deadening it works held together. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: the misplaced trust that shares the idol's deadness, reliance on nothing hollowing out the truster. Role (115) is characteristic - a standing trait of the idolater. Locus (116) here is recorded as 'paired with becoming like them' - the trust is set alongside the becoming-like-the-idols it produces. The full process, read at full weight in its descent: from no named source and no organ-seat, those who make idols with ears that cannot hear and no breath in their mouths, and all who trust in them, become like them - a misplaced disposition bound to an inner condition and paired with that deadening likeness: here, as at Psalm 115, the family's trust is read at its most futile, reliance on the breathless and lifeless that empties the one who relies, the truster taking on the very deadness of what he trusts.
narratives.story: Echoing an earlier psalm almost word for word, this one delivers the same verdict on idols and those who rely on them. The idols have ears but cannot hear, and there is no breath at all in their mouths - they are utterly dead. And then the line that turns on the worshipper: those who make them become like them; so do all who trust in them. To rely on lifeless things is to grow lifeless yourself. The trust is a settled bearing bent toward nothing, and it hollows the truster out to match the emptiness he leans on. The passage reads this misplaced reliance at full weight, as a kind of self-destruction. It is the sobering picture of what trusting dead things does to a living person - you come to resemble what you rely on, and to put your faith in the breathless is to have the breath drained out of you.
narratives.variation_note: Among the batach readings, this is a DESCENT-reading twinning Psa 115:8 - trust in breathless idols that renders the truster 'like them' (internal:ib-state) - reliance on the lifeless that hollows out the self, the futile counterpart to trust in the living God.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is sur - 'depart from me, you bloodthirsty men' - the interior act of severance, an aversive self-positioning. Type (102) is volition: an act of the will, a drawing of a line, not a felt state. Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior spring; the severance simply stands, its origin unfiled. Seat (104) resolves to none: the severance is not organ-located; the whole self acts, not a faculty. Bearer (105) is the psalmist (inferred): the interior that has just marvelled at being known and formed by God, and now recoils from the wicked. Operation (106), the core event, is that the self actively commands distance from bloodthirsty men, drawing a line. Target (107) is dissociation (inferred): the aim is the self's severance from evil company. Manner (108) is none - no mode is coloured. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no degree, no narrowing, no booked outcome. Coupling (112) is separate-from (inferred): the volition is welded to the act of separation. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: the interior act of severance - the self expels the company of evil, an aversive self-positioning. Role (115) is characteristic - a standing trait. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state: the severance is a condition of the inner being. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the psalmist who has just wondered at being wholly known and knitted together by God turns abruptly on the men of blood - 'depart from me' - a willed act of severance welded to the drawing of a line and held within as an inner state: intimacy with God issues at once in distance from evil, the self that rests in being known by God recoiling inwardly from the bloodthirsty and positioning itself away from them.
narratives.story: This psalm is one of the most intimate in the Bible - the writer marvelling that God knows him completely, formed him in the womb, and is always with him. And then, without warning, it turns hard: oh that you would slay the wicked, O God! O men of blood, depart from me! The very closeness to God that fills the psalm produces an instant recoil from evil. Having rested in being fully known and loved by God, the psalmist draws a sharp inner line against the bloodthirsty and pushes them away from himself. It is a deliberate act of the will, a self-positioning away from evil company. The passage sets the two side by side: nearness to God and distance from the wicked. It is the striking picture of how intimacy with God shapes a person's loyalties - the closer he is drawn to God, the more decisively he separates himself from those bent on harm.
narratives.variation_note: See the variation note at Psa 6:8 (H5493:depart#1). This third reading is an AVERSIVE SEVERANCE flowing from intimacy with God - having marvelled at being wholly known, the self recoils from the bloodthirsty and draws an inner line (internal:ib-state) - distinct from the lament-pivot of Psa 6:8 and the obedience-separation of Psa 119:115 (external:person).

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is chasah - 'my eyes are toward you; in you I seek refuge' - the interior orienting upward for shelter. Type (102) is affect: a movement of reliant feeling, not a bare deed. Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior spring; the refuge-seeking simply stands, its origin unfiled. Seat (104) resolves to none: the refuge is not organ-located; the whole self shelters, not a faculty. Bearer (105) is the psalmist (inferred): the interior guarding itself from the traps of evildoers. Operation (106), the core event, is that the eyes are fixed on God, seeking refuge, the self declining to be left defenceless. Target (107) is refuge-seeking (inferred): the aim is the sheltering, entrusting the exposed self. Manner (108) is none - no mode is coloured. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no degree, no narrowing, no booked outcome. Coupling (112) is eyes-toward-God (inferred): the affect is welded to the fixed gaze, the seeking and the upward look one movement. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: the interior orients upward for shelter, entrusting the exposed self. Role (115) is characteristic - a standing trait. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state: the refuge-seeking is a condition of the inner being. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the psalmist, ringed by the snares of evildoers, lifts his eyes to God and seeks refuge in him, pleading not to be left defenceless - a movement of reliant feeling welded to the fixed upward gaze and held within as an inner state: refuge here takes the form of the lifted eyes, the exposed self entrusting itself to God by simply looking to him, sheltering in the direction of its gaze.
narratives.story: Hemmed in by the traps and snares of evildoers, the psalmist describes the one direction he keeps looking: my eyes are toward you, O God, my Lord; in you I seek refuge; leave me not defenceless. His refuge takes the form of a gaze - he shelters in God by keeping his eyes fixed on him. Exposed and surrounded, he entrusts his vulnerable self upward, refusing to be left without protection. The seeking and the looking are one movement; to take cover here is simply to keep looking to God. The passage does not add anything further; it shows a threatened man whose whole security is bound up in where he turns his eyes. It is the quiet picture of trust as attention - a person in danger who, instead of watching the traps around him, fixes his gaze on God and finds his shelter in that upward look.
narratives.variation_note: The item H2620:refug (chasah, the noun-like 'refuge'/take refuge) has four readings: Psa 57:1 (twice), 91:4 and 141:8. This fourth reading (Psa 141:8) takes refuge the form of the LIFTED EYES - 'my eyes are toward you; in you I seek refuge' - sheltering as attention, the exposed self entrusting itself by its gaze (internal:ib-state), distinct from the fugitive's soul-flight (Psa 57:1) and the promised nestling under wings (Psa 91:4).

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is machseh - 'You are my refuge, my portion in the land of the living' - the self fastening onto God against total abandonment. Type (102) is affect: a movement of reliant feeling, not a bare deed. Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior spring; the re-grounding simply stands, its origin unfiled. Seat (104) resolves to none: the refuge is not organ-located; the whole self shelters, not a faculty. Bearer (105) is the psalmist (inferred): the interior in the cave, crying that no one cares for his soul. Operation (106), the core event, is that against abandonment the self declares God its refuge and portion among the living. Target (107) is re-grounding (inferred): the aim is the fastening of the whole self onto God as its share. Manner (108) is none - no mode is coloured. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no degree, no narrowing, no booked outcome. Coupling (112) is you-are-my-portion (inferred): the affect is welded to God named as portion, refuge and share one declaration. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: the interior answers isolation by fastening the whole self onto God as its share. Role (115) is characteristic - a standing trait. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state: the refuge is a condition of the inner being. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the psalmist, hidden in a cave and convinced that no one takes notice of him or cares for his soul, answers that emptiness by fastening onto God - 'you are my refuge, my portion in the land of the living' - a movement of reliant feeling welded to God named as his portion and held within as an inner state: exactly where he says no refuge remains to him among men, he finds his refuge and his whole share in God, the abandoned self re-grounded on the one who is left when everyone else has failed.
narratives.story: This prayer comes from a man at the end of his resources, hidden in a cave, crying out that no one takes notice of him and no one cares for his soul - no refuge remains to me, he says. And then, in the very place where every human shelter has run out, he turns and fastens onto God: I say, You are my refuge, my portion in the land of the living. Exactly where he has just said there is no refuge left, he finds one - in God. God becomes not only his hiding-place but his whole share, the portion he has among the living when everyone else has failed him. The passage lets the isolation and the re-grounding sit side by side. It is the moving picture of an utterly abandoned person discovering that when every other refuge is gone, God himself is the one that remains.
narratives.variation_note: The item H4268:refug (machseh, 'refuge') has three readings: Psa 73:28, 91:2 and 142:5. This third machseh reading is refuge found AGAINST TOTAL ABANDONMENT - in the cave, 'no refuge remains to me... You are my refuge, my portion' (internal:ib-state) - the self re-grounded on God exactly where every human shelter has failed, distinct from the deliberate choice of Psa 73:28 and the settled confession of Psa 91:2.

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is batach - 'let me hear of your steadfast love in the morning, for in you I trust' - reliance that times its hope to the dawn. Type (102) is affect: a movement of reliant feeling, not a bare deed. Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior spring; the trust simply stands, its origin unfiled. Seat (104) resolves to none: the trust is not organ-located; the whole self relies, not a faculty. Bearer (105) is the psalmist (inferred): the failing interior whose spirit faints and whose heart is appalled. Operation (106), the core event, is that the self entrusts itself, asking to hear steadfast love at daybreak - trust grounded in leaning its weight on God. Target (107) is entrustment (inferred): the aim is the handing-over of the self to God. Manner (108) is none - no mode is coloured. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no degree, no narrowing, no booked outcome. Coupling (112) is trust-at-morning (inferred): the affect is welded to the timing of the dawn, reliance and the awaited morning one. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: the interior leans its weight on God, timing hope to the dawn. Role (115) is characteristic - a standing trait. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state: the trust is a condition of the inner being. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the psalmist whose spirit faints and whose heart is appalled leans his weight on God and asks to hear of his steadfast love in the morning - 'for in you I trust' - a movement of reliant feeling welded to the awaited dawn and held within as an inner state: here trust reaches through the dark toward daybreak, the failing self entrusting itself to God and timing its hope to the morning, asking that the first thing the new day brings be word of God's covenant love.
narratives.story: This is a prayer from the edge of despair - the writer's spirit fainting, his heart appalled, his enemy having crushed his life to the ground. Reaching through the darkness toward morning, he asks: let me hear in the morning of your steadfast love, for in you I trust. His trust times itself to the dawn; he leans his failing weight on God and asks that the first thing the new day brings be word of God's faithful love. Even at his lowest, worn down and nearly out of strength, he hands himself over to God and waits for daybreak. The passage holds the exhaustion and the trust together. It is the tender picture of faith in the dark - a person barely holding on who cannot see any light yet, but who entrusts himself to God through the night and asks only to hear, when morning comes, that he is still loved.
narratives.variation_note: Among the batach readings, this one TIMES trust to the dawn - the failing self entrusting itself and asking to hear of steadfast love 'in the morning' (internal:ib-state) - reliance reaching through the dark toward daybreak, distinct from settled trust (Psa 84:12) or trust met at once by help (Psa 28:7).

narratives.narrative: The sense (101) is batach - 'put not your trust in princes, in a son of man' - the deliberate withdrawal of reliance from mortal power. Type (102) is volition: an act of the will, a redirecting, not a mere feeling. Source (103) is absent: the reading books no interior spring; the warning simply stands, its origin unfiled. Seat (104) resolves to none: the trust is not organ-located; the whole self relies, not a faculty. Bearer (105) is the psalmist (inferred): the interior, and the hearer, warned off leaning on mortal man. Operation (106), the core event, is that the self is warned off trusting princes and mortal man, redirecting reliance to God. Target (107) is trust-redirection (inferred): the aim is the moving of reliance from man to God. Manner (108) is none - no mode is coloured. Intensity (109), specifier (110) and effect (111) are absent: no degree, no narrowing, no booked outcome. Coupling (112) is trust-not-princes (inferred): the volition is welded to the refusal of princes, the redirection defined by what it rejects. Prohibition (113) is absent. Discovery (114) names it: the deliberate withdrawal of reliance from mortal power - princes in whom there is no salvation. Role (115) is characteristic - a standing trait. Locus (116) is internal:ib-state: the trust is a condition of the inner being. The full process: from no named source and no organ-seat, the psalmist charges the self to pull its trust off princes and mortal man - in whom there is no salvation, whose breath departs and whose plans perish that very day - and to redirect it to the God of Jacob, whose help and hope do not fail: a willed redirection welded to the refusal of princes and held within as an inner state; the psalm blesses instead the one whose help is the God of Jacob, so that the withdrawal from mortal power is the negative face of a trust meant to land wholly on God.
narratives.story: This psalm of praise pauses to give a sharp warning: put not your trust in princes, in a son of man, in whom there is no salvation. The reason follows at once - when a ruler's breath departs, he returns to the earth, and on that very day his plans die with him. Mortal power cannot save; it is here today and gone tomorrow. So the psalmist tells the self to pull its reliance off princes and mortal man deliberately. And the warning has a positive other half: blessed instead is the one whose help is the God of Jacob, whose hope is in the Lord - the God who made everything and keeps faith forever. The passage moves trust off the failing and onto the everlasting. It is the clear-eyed picture of redirecting your confidence - taking it off human powers that die and placing it on the God who does not.
narratives.variation_note: Among the batach readings, this is a willed REDIRECTION (volition) - trust pulled off dying princes and mortal man 'in whom there is no salvation' and turned toward the God of Jacob (internal:ib-state) - the descent-warning that is the negative face of true trust, kin to Psa 118:9 (princes) but framed as an act of the will.
